Root cause: babbitt distress from degraded oil film due to water ingress via a leaking lube-oil cooler tube, undetected without online water-in-oil monitoring.

P2 Repair cooler tube — 30-Apr-2026 — STA-02 — Closed · X1 Install online water-in-oil sensor on KO-3201 — 30-Jun-2026 — REL-05 — In Progress · P2 Retube cooler at next TA — 31-Oct-2026 — STA-02 — Open · X1 Online water-in-oil monitoring on KO-3202/3203 — 30-Sep-2026 — REL-05 — Open

X3 Tighten KO-3201 vibration alert to 45 micron & shorten trend-review cadence — 30-May-2026 — REL-05 · X2 Add cooler dP & conductivity trend to reliability dashboard — 30-Jun-2026 — REL-02. Risk countermeasure: start-up alarm suppression timer — 30-May-2026. PM-1 weekly water/particle count; PM-2 6-monthly cooler leak test; PM-3 daily vibration trend review.

26 weekly readings · downtime 32 h · availability 99.27 % (period 4,368 h) · ALARM 11 · TRIP 1 · NORMAL 14 · PM compliance 92 % · production loss 1,760 t · estimated loss 1,584 k USD (production loss × product price).
Design Life: 5 years (bearing) / 24 months (seal element). The same value appears on all five equipment files.

Vibration alert threshold version: A (EV-10) Alert was 60 micron before the trip / B (EV-02) Equipment Info lists alarm 45 micron (no effective date). Slide 10 plans tightening the alert to 45 micron by 30-May-2026, so Equipment Info may show the post-change limit. Effective date is not recorded; historical ALARM labels cannot be assumed to use 45.

When vibration started rising: A (EV-07) RCA: rise from 28 to 52 micron over ~5 days before 27 Apr / B (EV-03) Weekly record: 71.7 micron on 22 Apr, ALARM since 11 Feb. The hourly PI series (EV-06) agrees with the RCA's late rise (≈29 until 26 Apr). Weekly and hourly series may come from different measurement points or definitions; the weekly replay must not be called an operational reconstruction.

How long water content exceeded 500 ppm: A (EV-08) RCA: above 500 ppm for ~2 weeks / B (EV-03) Weekly record: above 500 ppm from 11 Feb (~11 weeks). Matters for the effectiveness rule of the water-in-oil monitoring action: which sampling record is authoritative?

Lube-oil supply pressure at failure: A (EV-09) RCA 4P: header pressure 1.8 barg, within normal band (G) / B (EV-04) Weekly record: 1.078 barg at trip week, below the 1.1 trip limit. If the weekly value is valid, P3 'G' would need re-assessment. Possibly different measurement point (header vs bearing supply).

Bearing design life: A (EV-09) RCA 4P: 6-year design / B (EV-14) Equipment Info: 5 years (bearing). Both sources agree the bearing (3 years in service) was within life. Equipment Info carries an identical design-life string for all five assets, which suggests a template default.

Vibration units: weekly micron vs hourly MM/S: A (EV-03) Weekly DE Radial Vibration in micron / B (EV-06) PI tag KO3201_VIB engineering unit MM/S, values 25–73. Displacement (micron) and velocity (mm/s) are not convertible without frequency content. The PI magnitudes resemble micron values, so the PI unit label itself needs confirmation. Rule applied: never overlay or convert.

Run status OFF with non-zero current: A (EV-06) RUN_STATUS = OFF for 32 h / B (EV-06) KO3201_AMP 3.9–4.6 A while OFF. Values kept as recorded (all 85 OFF rows in the five files behave the same). Sensor semantics must be confirmed before any energy conversion.

shows.text: Weekly condition records labelled KO-3201 ALARM every week from 11 Feb to 22 Apr 2026, while lube-oil water content rose from 501 to 1,373 ppm and DE vibration from 37.7 to 71.7 micron.
The compressor tripped on 29 Apr 2026. The register records 32 h downtime, US$1,584,000 actual loss and US$475,200 potential loss, with incident status CA/PA EXECUTION.
All five weekly readings after the repair (6 May – 3 Jun 2026) are NORMAL. No condition reading after 3 Jun 2026 exists in the snapshot.

documented_findings.text: The RCA attributes the trip to journal-bearing babbitt distress from degraded oil-film strength, caused by water ingress through a leaking lube-oil cooler tube and left undetected because there was no online water-in-oil monitoring.
The cooler tube leak and the wiped babbitt were confirmed at strip-down on 29 Apr; lab water content was 1,800 ppm against a < 500 ppm spec.

The immediate repair (plug and re-test of the cooler tube) is recorded Closed. The KO-3201 online water-in-oil sensor is recorded In Progress with a plan date of 30 Jun 2026; the cooler retube (31 Oct 2026) and the KO-3202/3203 roll-out (30 Sep 2026) are recorded Open.
Two preventive actions on slide 10 (vibration alert to 45 micron by 30 May; cooler dP and conductivity trending by 30 Jun) carry plan dates but no status at all.

hypotheses.text: Low lube-oil supply pressure may have contributed to the oil-film breakdown, in addition to water contamination.
missing: Which pressure point each record measures (header vs bearing supply)
Lube-oil filter dP and pump discharge history

conflicts_missing.text: The vibration alert threshold has two versions (60 micron in the RCA, 45 micron in Equipment Info) and no effective date, so it is unclear which limit applied before the trip.

The sources disagree on when the deterioration became visible. The weekly record shows ALARM from 11 Feb, while the RCA and the hourly PI series show the vibration rise only in the last days before the trip.
The RCA rates supply pressure as normal (1.8 barg), but the weekly record shows 1.078 barg in the trip week.
No record shows that the online water-in-oil sensor has been installed or commissioned. Status was In Progress at the snapshot and the plan date (30 Jun 2026) is before the review date.
The source files carry no publication or update time, so the snapshot statuses may be older than the review date.

verify_next.text: Confirm the installation, commissioning and signal validation of the KO-3201 online water-in-oil sensor.
verify_next.why: It is the control for root cause X1, and its plan date has passed. Machine recovery does not show that it exists.

verify_next.text: Confirm whether the vibration alert was changed to 45 micron, and when.
verify_next.why: Threshold history decides how past ALARM labels should be read and whether preventive action X3 is done.

verify_next.text: Reconcile the supply-pressure records and re-check the P3 'G' assessment.
verify_next.why: If the weekly 1.078 barg is valid, the 4P table understates a contributing condition.

verify_next.text: Confirm the status of the KO-3202/3203 monitoring roll-out.
verify_next.why: Its plan date (30 Sep 2026) has passed and the source records it as Open.

verify_next.text: Confirm that the cooler retube is in the scope of the next turnaround.
verify_next.why: It is not yet due (31 Oct 2026). The check is about its scheduling, not about lateness.

shows.text: Lube-oil water content crossed its 500 ppm alarm limit on 11 Feb 2026 and rose every week to 1,373 ppm on 22 Apr (trip limit 1,500 ppm).
Over the same weeks DE radial vibration rose from 37.7 to 71.7 micron (trip 75) and bearing metal temperature from 84.9 to 107.1 °C (trip 110).
Lube-oil supply pressure fell from 1.635 to 1.122 barg, just above the 1.1 barg trip limit.
The hourly PI vibration tag (unit MM/S) stays between 28 and 30 throughout 1–22 Apr and does not show the rise seen in the weekly record.

hypotheses.text: Lubrication degradation from water-contaminated lube oil is reducing bearing oil-film capacity, which would explain the rise in bearing temperature and vibration together.
missing: Lab oil analysis (Karl Fischer water, viscosity, free water)

hypotheses.text: The water source is not identifiable from these inputs. Candidates include a lube-oil cooler leak, condensation or seal/buffer-gas ingress, and contaminated make-up oil.
missing: Cooler leak test, or oil-side vs cooling-water conductivity

hypotheses.text: The falling supply pressure may be a separate lube-system fault (filter fouling, pump wear) rather than a consequence of contamination.
missing: Filter dP and pump discharge pressure history

conflicts_missing.text: The weekly vibration record (micron) and the hourly PI tag (MM/S) disagree in both trend and unit, so they must not be merged. Which one represents the DE bearing probe is unknown.
None of the limits has an effective date, so it is unknown whether the current ALARM labels used these exact limits.
